description: Operation Israel continues as Redcult takes down a list of Israeli websites in advance of Eid al-Adha, an important Muslim holiday celebrated at the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Occupied Palestine. Also known as the "Feast of Sacrifice", it takes place over a four day period and is celebrated worldwide, making it the 2nd most important event in the Muslim calendar.

faqs.answer: #OpAqsa is a component of #OpIsrael in which the Anonymous group Redcult targeted 41 Israeli government websites as a "gentle reminder" to respect the Muslim holiday of Eid al-Adha, celebrated at the Al-Aqsa Mosque in occupied Jerusalem.
faqs.question: What is Operation Al-Aqsa (#OpAqsa)?

faqs.answer: Eid al-Adha, the "Feast of Sacrifice," is the second most important holiday in the Muslim calendar, celebrated over four days. It is deeply connected to the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem, which is the third holiest site in Islam.
faqs.question: What is Eid al-Adha?

faqs.answer: Redcult announced they had taken down 41 Israeli government websites as part of #OpAqsa, releasing a full list of the affected domains.
faqs.question: How many Israeli websites did Redcult target?

faqs.answer: The Al-Aqsa Mosque compound (Temple Mount/Haram al-Sharif) in Jerusalem is the third holiest site in Islam and has been the site of recurring violence and political tension between Israeli forces and Palestinian worshippers, particularly during Muslim holidays.
faqs.question: What is the historical significance of the Al-Aqsa Mosque?
